> `cwcli init` no longer spends minutes aligning the container user to your host, a new `cwcli doctor` command checks whether your machine can run cwcli at all, and cwcli finds benches it used to miss.

### New Features

* `cwcli doctor` (and `cwcli axi doctor`) checks whether cwcli can operate on this machine at all: Docker and Docker Compose, cwcli's own config and cache directories, free disk space, transfer and Git-hosting tooling, and port ranges colliding across your instances. A warning exits 0, so it stays safe to chain in a script; a failure exits non-zero

### Bug Fixes

* Docker Desktop stopped on WSL2 is no longer reported as "not installed" - cwcli now tells you to start Docker Desktop instead of pointing at the install page
* `restore --send` checks for free disk space before staging files, the same check `--receive` already had, instead of failing with a cryptic transfer error on a full disk
* `cwcli init` and `cwcli scale` check that the Docker Compose plugin is present before touching anything, instead of failing partway through with a raw error
* `cwcli inspect` now finds a bench created by hand directly under the container's workspace, which it previously missed entirely
* `cwcli open`'s interactive Docker shell no longer fights the calling console for keystrokes on Windows

### Performance Improvements

* `cwcli init` aligning the container user to your host account now takes seconds instead of minutes
